statement: raw.issue_type exposes an is_subtask column that can be selected directly.
evidence_of_dependence: description,is_subtask is_subtask from raw.issue_type
alternative: The DESCRIBE result lists "subtask", not "is_subtask".
reason: The generated SQL depends on this column being available to execute.

statement: The underscore-prefixed issue estimate and time-spent fields should take precedence over their unprefixed counterparts whenever both are populated.
evidence_of_dependence: coalesce(_original_estimate,original_estimate); coalesce(_remaining_estimate,remaining_estimate); coalesce(_time_spent,time_spent)
alternative: The index exposes both versions of each field, while the contract names only the output fields and does not specify precedence.
reason: Conflicting source values would change all three effort measures.

statement: Both versions of each raw issue estimate and time-spent field already contain seconds.
evidence_of_dependence: cast(coalesce(_time_spent,time_spent) as double) time_spent_seconds
reason: A different source unit would systematically scale downstream effort measures incorrectly.

statement: Every retained issue has created and updated values that TRY_CAST can convert to non-null timestamps.
evidence_of_dependence: try_cast(created as timestamp) created_at, ... try_cast(updated as timestamp) updated_at ... where ... created is not null and updated is not null
alternative: The contract requires both "created_at" and "updated_at" to be not_null, whereas the filters test only the source strings.
reason: Non-null malformed strings would survive filtering but violate required output constraints.

statement: Every retained issue has a non-null key.
evidence_of_dependence: cast(key as varchar) issue_key ... where id is not null and created is not null and updated is not null and project is not null
alternative: The contract gives "issue_key" a not_null constraint.
reason: The SQL does not validate this required attribute.

statement: For repeated issue IDs, descending lexical order of updated selects the authoritative record, with any ties interchangeable.
evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over(partition by id order by updated desc nulls last)=1
reason: The source column is VARCHAR, so formatting differences or conflicting ties could select a different issue state.

statement: Version IDs require no whitespace correction beyond rejecting whitespace-only values.
evidence_of_dependence: cast(id as varchar) version_id ... where id is not null and trim(id)<>''
alternative: The contract explicitly requires "version_id = TRIM(version_id)" with on_failure: correct.
reason: Uncorrected identifiers can violate the contract and fail downstream matches.

statement: Direct TRY_CAST to TIMESTAMP correctly normalizes all supported version date formats, including timezone suffixes.
evidence_of_dependence: try_cast(release_date as timestamp) release_date,try_cast(start_date as timestamp) start_date
alternative: The contract explicitly calls for correction of date strings matching ".*\\+.{4}$" before accepting valid timestamps.
reason: Unsupported but correctable date strings could be silently nullified instead of normalized.

statement: Version IDs are unique among the retained source rows.
evidence_of_dependence: from raw.version where id is not null and trim(id)<>'' and name is not null and trim(name)<>''
alternative: The contract requires "version_id" to be unique.
reason: No uniqueness check or deduplication is performed.

statement: archived and released need no correction to yield acceptable is_archived and is_released values.
evidence_of_dependence: archived is_archived,released is_released
alternative: The contract requires "is_archived IN (TRUE,FALSE)" and "is_released IN (TRUE,FALSE)" with on_failure: correct; DESCRIBE reports nullable BOOLEAN source columns.
reason: The types establish boolean representation but do not establish the absence of null values requiring a policy.

statement: User IDs are unique among source rows with non-null IDs.
evidence_of_dependence: from raw.user where id is not null
alternative: The contract requires "user_id" to be unique.
reason: Duplicate accounts would remain and could multiply downstream joins.

statement: Replacing a missing or whitespace-only user display name with the user ID is an acceptable correction.
evidence_of_dependence: coalesce(nullif(trim(name), ''), cast(id as varchar)) user_display_name
alternative: The contract requires a not_null display name but does not authorize ID substitution; the general quality actions include deletion for "Essential business attributes contain irrecoverable errors".
reason: This policy retains accounts with invented display-name values rather than another handling of invalid names.

statement: Trimming nonempty user display names is part of the required naming standardization.
evidence_of_dependence: nullif(trim(name), '')
reason: The description suggests consistent naming but does not prescribe this specific alteration.

statement: Repeated project IDs have interchangeable attribute values, so an arbitrary retained row is sufficient.
evidence_of_dependence: qualify row_number() over(partition by id order by id)=1
reason: Ordering by the partition key does not resolve conflicting project records.

statement: Every component row with a non-null ID also has a non-null name.
evidence_of_dependence: name component_name ... from raw.component where id is not null
alternative: The contract requires "component_name" to be not_null.
reason: The SQL omits validation of a required attribute.

statement: Repeated component IDs have interchangeable attribute values.
evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over(partition by id order by id)=1
reason: Conflicting duplicates would be resolved arbitrarily.

statement: Every field definition with a non-null ID has a non-null name.
evidence_of_dependence: name field_name ... from raw.field where id is not null
alternative: The contract requires "field_name" to be not_null.
reason: Required field metadata is not validated.

statement: Repeated field IDs have interchangeable names and metadata flags.
evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over(partition by id order by id)=1
reason: Arbitrary duplicate selection could change field interpretation downstream.

statement: Every issue type with a non-null ID has a non-null name.
evidence_of_dependence: name issue_type_name ... where id is not null
alternative: The contract requires "issue_type_name" to be not_null.
reason: The query does not validate the required name.

statement: Repeated issue-type IDs have interchangeable attribute values.
evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over(partition by id order by id)=1
reason: Conflicting duplicate definitions would be resolved arbitrarily.

statement: Every priority with a non-null ID has a non-null name.
evidence_of_dependence: name priority_name ... from raw.priority where id is not null
alternative: The contract requires "priority_name" to be not_null.
reason: The required name constraint is not enforced.

statement: Repeated priority IDs have interchangeable attribute values.
evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over(partition by id order by id)=1
reason: Conflicting priority definitions would be resolved arbitrarily.

statement: Every resolution with a non-null ID has a non-null name.
evidence_of_dependence: name resolution_name ... from raw.resolution where id is not null
alternative: The contract requires "resolution_name" to be not_null.
reason: The required name constraint is not enforced.

statement: Repeated resolution IDs have interchangeable attribute values.
evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over(partition by id order by id)=1
reason: Conflicting resolution definitions would be resolved arbitrarily.

statement: Every status category with a non-null ID has a non-null name.
evidence_of_dependence: name status_category_name ... from raw.status_category where id is not null
alternative: The contract requires "status_category_name" to be not_null.
reason: The required name constraint is not enforced.

statement: Repeated status-category IDs have interchangeable names.
evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over(partition by id order by id)=1
reason: Conflicting category names would be resolved arbitrarily.

statement: Every status with a non-null ID has a non-null name.
evidence_of_dependence: name status_name ... from raw.status where id is not null
alternative: The contract requires "status_name" to be not_null.
reason: The required name constraint is not enforced.

statement: Repeated status IDs have interchangeable names, descriptions, and category IDs.
evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over(partition by id order by id)=1
reason: An arbitrary category assignment could affect downstream lifecycle classification.

statement: Sprint IDs are unique among retained source rows.
evidence_of_dependence: from raw.sprint where id is not null and trim(id)<>'' and name is not null and trim(name)<>''
alternative: The contract requires "sprint_id" to be unique.
reason: There is no deduplication or uniqueness validation.

statement: Direct TRY_CAST preserves all valid sprint dates with the intended timestamp meaning.
evidence_of_dependence: try_cast(start_date as timestamp) started_at, try_cast(end_date as timestamp) ended_at, try_cast(complete_date as timestamp) completed_at
reason: Unverified string formats could silently erase dates used for sprint analytics.

statement: All retained comment created values convert to non-null timestamps.
evidence_of_dependence: try_cast(created as timestamp) created_at ... where ... created is not null
alternative: The contract requires "created_at" to be not_null, not merely its source string.
reason: Malformed non-null strings would survive as invalid required output values.

statement: For repeated comment IDs, retaining the row with the lexically earliest created value selects the appropriate comment version, with ties interchangeable.
evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over(partition by id order by created)=1
reason: Duplicate records could contain different bodies or updates that this ordering does not reconcile.

statement: Every retained issue-field-history time converts to a non-null timestamp.
evidence_of_dependence: try_cast(time as timestamp) updated_at ... and time is not null
alternative: The contract requires "updated_at" to be not_null.
reason: The source-string check does not ensure valid required timestamps.

statement: Every retained issue-field-history row has a non-null is_active value.
evidence_of_dependence: cast(value as varchar) field_value,is_active ... where field_id is not null and issue_id is not null and time is not null
alternative: The contract requires "is_active" to be not_null; DESCRIBE reports a nullable source BOOLEAN.
reason: The query does not handle missing activity flags.

statement: Every retained multiselect-history time converts to a non-null timestamp.
evidence_of_dependence: try_cast(time as timestamp) updated_at ... and time is not null
alternative: The contract requires "updated_at" to be not_null.
reason: Malformed source strings could violate the required output constraint.

statement: Every retained multiselect-history row has a non-null is_active value.
evidence_of_dependence: cast(value as varchar) field_value,is_active ... where field_id is not null and issue_id is not null and time is not null
alternative: The contract requires "is_active" to be not_null; DESCRIBE reports a nullable source BOOLEAN.
reason: The query does not handle missing activity flags.

statement: The inward issue is the intended issue_id and the outward issue is the intended related_issue_id in the staging link representation.
evidence_of_dependence: inward_issue_id as varchar) issue_id,cast(outward_issue_id as varchar) related_issue_id
reason: The contract names the output endpoints without defining their direction, which can affect directional relationship analysis.

statement: Averaging only issues with valid assignment durations is equivalent to dividing duration sums by all closed or open assigned issues, respectively.
evidence_of_dependence: round(avg(epoch(resolved_at)-epoch(last_assigned_at)) filter(where resolved_at is not null and last_assigned_at is not null)) ac
alternative: The contract says to "divide the sum of close durations by the closed issue count" and specifies the analogous denominator for open issues, including issues without valid durations.
reason: Mixed missing and valid assignment timestamps would change both user averages and their day conversions.

statement: Leaving the original parent_issue_id unchanged and exposing the revised parent only as parent_issue_id_derived satisfies the required parent identifier interface.
evidence_of_dependence: select i.*,coalesce(i.revised_parent_issue_id,i.parent_issue_id) parent_issue_id_derived
alternative: The contract requires "Derive parent_issue_id by taking revised_parent_issue_id when present; otherwise use the original parent_issue_id".
reason: Issues linked through Epic history would expose the original rather than revised parent under the required column name.

statement: The duplicate source columns issue_id_1 and parent_issue_id_1 are unnecessary in the issue-users output.
evidence_of_dependence: select i.*,coalesce(i.revised_parent_issue_id,i.parent_issue_id) parent_issue_id_derived
alternative: The contract explicitly says the output "includes duplicate source versions named issue_id_1 and parent_issue_id_1".
reason: Consumers expecting the documented columns would not receive the required schema.

statement: A NULL is_active_sprint value is acceptable when the joined sprint has no start timestamp.
evidence_of_dependence: (sp.sprint_started_at<=current_timestamp and (sp.sprint_completed_at is null or sp.sprint_completed_at>=current_timestamp)) is_active_sprint
alternative: The contract requires true when the start timestamp is present and the timing conditions hold, and "otherwise false".
reason: Issues without a matched sprint can receive NULL instead of the required false.

statement: Every matched version ID is already in the canonical decimal-string form produced by casting an integer to VARCHAR.
evidence_of_dependence: on cast(l.version_id as varchar)=ver.version_id
alternative: The contract says to "Convert field_value to an integer version_id and join to the version table"; numerically equivalent version IDs such as zero-padded strings could instead be matched numerically.
reason: Noncanonical textual version IDs could silently remove version names from the aggregates.

statement: Silently converting non-integer version-history values to NULL is acceptable.
evidence_of_dependence: try_cast(field_value as integer) version_id
alternative: The contract specifies conversion to an integer but does not prescribe silent rejection of invalid or out-of-range values.
reason: Invalid version references would disappear rather than trigger another required handling policy.

statement: All project duration inputs are chronologically ordered so that calculated average and median durations are non-negative.
evidence_of_dependence: epoch(resolved_at)-epoch(created_at); epoch(last_assigned_at)-epoch(first_assigned_at); epoch(current_timestamp)-epoch(first_assigned_at)
alternative: The contract requires non-negative averages and tests each median with "IS NULL OR ... >= 0".
reason: Future or reversed timestamps could violate multiple required metric constraints without any handling in this model.

statement: Converting unrounded project medians directly to days always gives the same result as converting the rounded seconds metrics.
evidence_of_dependence: round(med_close/86400) median_close_time_days ... round(med_close) median_close_time_seconds
alternative: The contract says days metrics "convert the corresponding seconds metric to days by dividing by 86400 and rounding".
reason: Fractional-second medians near half-day boundaries can produce different day values.

statement: Project count metrics may retain DuckDB COUNT's BIGINT type instead of the documented HUGEINT type.
evidence_of_dependence: count(*) filter(where resolved_at is not null) count_closed_issues
alternative: The contract declares the three output count columns as "data_type: HUGEINT".
reason: The generated output schema depends on treating explicit contract types as optional.

statement: Project duration metrics may retain their inferred floating-point types instead of DECIMAL(18,0).
evidence_of_dependence: round(coalesce(close_sum/nullif(count_closed_issues,0),0)) avg_close_s
alternative: The contract declares the seconds and days duration metrics as "data_type: DECIMAL(18,0)".
reason: Rounding floating-point expressions does not establish the required decimal output schema.

statement: User count metrics may retain DuckDB COUNT's BIGINT type instead of HUGEINT.
evidence_of_dependence: count(*) filter(where resolved_at is not null) count_closed_issues
alternative: The contract declares count_closed_issues and count_open_issues as "data_type: HUGEINT".
reason: The output does not explicitly implement the documented count types.

statement: User duration metrics may retain their inferred floating-point types instead of DECIMAL(18,0).
evidence_of_dependence: round(median(epoch(resolved_at)-epoch(last_assigned_at)) filter(where resolved_at is not null and last_assigned_at is not null)) mc
alternative: The contract declares the duration outputs as "data_type: DECIMAL(18,0)".
reason: Whole-valued floating-point results do not provide the required decimal schema.

statement: At least one sprint survives staging validation.
evidence_of_dependence: left join s on s.seq=mod(i.h,sn.n)+1
alternative: The contract states "At least one sprint is required; if there are no sprints, this model will error", but the SQL does not explicitly enforce that failure.
reason: An empty sprint set would prevent the promised one-sprint mapping and may not produce the required error.

statement: Sprint health scores may be fixed at 100 without applying the documented penalties and bonuses.
evidence_of_dependence: 100::integer sprint_health_score
alternative: The contract says to "subtract 30 if Behind Schedule", apply additional penalties and bonuses, and "clamp to [0,100]".
reason: The constant bypasses the entire sprint health scoring calculation.

statement: All qualifying sprint issues have a latest active story-point value that is missing, unparsable, or numerically equal to 1.
evidence_of_dependence: i.time_spent_seconds,1.0 points from snapshots s join staging.stg_jira__issue i
alternative: The contract requires the "latest active field value whose field name contains ‘story’ and ‘point’" and defaults to 1 only when unavailable or unparsable.
reason: Ignoring field definitions and history can change nearly every story-point-based metric and classification.

statement: Applying the global 1000-row limit after joining issues to snapshots is equivalent to limiting sprint-issue pairs before generating snapshots.
evidence_of_dependence: from snapshots s join staging.stg_jira__issue i ... limit 1000
alternative: The contract applies "a global LIMIT 1000" to sprint_issues and subsequently generates start and end snapshots.
reason: Duplicated snapshot rows consume the limit and can leave snapshots with different issue populations or omit them entirely.

statement: Velocity trends may be left NULL instead of calculating their moving average.
evidence_of_dependence: null::double velocity_trend_3d
alternative: The contract defines velocity_trend_3d as the "moving average of daily_velocity over up to the last three snapshots in the sprint".
reason: The placeholder removes a required analytic measure even where valid velocities exist.

statement: Truncating issue creation timestamps to dates preserves sprint-window membership.
evidence_of_dependence: cast(i.created_at as date) between s.start_date and coalesce(s.completed_at,s.ended_at,current_timestamp)
alternative: The contract requires "issue.created_at falls between sprint.started_at and coalesce(sprint.completed_at, sprint.ended_at, current_timestamp)".
reason: Issues created before an intraday sprint start can be included incorrectly.

statement: Every project receives 25 in each health dimension under the documented scoring rules.
evidence_of_dependence: 25::integer delivery_health_score,25::integer quality_health_score,25::integer team_health_score,25::integer process_health_score
alternative: The contract specifies deductions for backlog, velocity, throughput, quality, resources, workload, sprint participation, links, and priority presence.
reason: Hard-coded dimension scores determine the overall score, grade, and primary risk without evaluating project conditions.

statement: None of the five documented project risk conditions is true for any project.
evidence_of_dependence: 0::integer backlog_risk,0::integer velocity_risk,0::integer quality_risk,0::integer resource_risk,0::integer throughput_risk
alternative: The contract requires each flag to be evaluated, including "resource_risk = 1 if unique_assignees < 2".
reason: All risk indicators are suppressed irrespective of the aggregate metrics already calculated.

statement: No project has issue creations or resolutions in any of the specified recent reporting windows.
evidence_of_dependence: 0::bigint issues_resolved_30d,0::bigint issues_created_30d,0::bigint issues_resolved_7d,0::bigint issues_resolved_prev_30d
alternative: The contract requires counts for the last 30 days, last 7 days, and the preceding 60–30-day resolution window.
reason: The constants discard required velocity and throughput information without examining timestamps.

statement: No project issue has any comments.
evidence_of_dependence: null::double avg_comments_per_issue
alternative: The contract requires averaging per-issue comment counts over issues with at least one comment and permits NULL only "if none".
reason: The unused comment source may contain information necessary for a required quality metric.

statement: No project issue participates in an issue link.
evidence_of_dependence: 0::bigint total_issue_links
alternative: The contract defines this indicator as "1 if any project issue participates in any issue link, else 0".
reason: The unused issue-link source can change the process-health inputs for whole projects.

statement: Each issue has at most one retained consecutive field-change interval.
evidence_of_dependence: from h join a using(issue_id) where h.previous_change_time is not null
alternative: The contract requires total_field_changes to be the "count of retained changes (number of consecutive intervals)", not a count after joining intervals back to changes only by issue_id.
reason: Multiple intervals produce a many-to-many join that squares their count and can change risk classifications and standard deviation.

statement: The documented standard deviation for activity_variance is the sample standard deviation.
evidence_of_dependence: stddev_samp(days_between_changes) activity_variance
alternative: The contract says "standard deviation of days_between_changes" without specifying sample or population.
reason: The choice affects small interval sets and determines whether a single interval yields NULL or zero.

statement: Explicit ascending issue_id ordering is unnecessary for the lifecycle result.
evidence_of_dependence: from b left join s using(issue_id)
alternative: The contract says "the final result is ordered by issue_id ascending".
reason: The query ends without implementing the required final ordering.

statement: An unchanged field on a pivot date may be represented by the literal is_null.
evidence_of_dependence: coalesce(status,'is_null') status,coalesce(sprint,'is_null') sprint,coalesce(story_points,'is_null') story_points
alternative: The contract says "Unchanged fields on that date remain NULL; fields changed to true NULL appear as ‘is_null’".
reason: Coalescing after the pivot erases the distinction between no update and an explicit null update, disrupting downstream forward-fill.

statement: For a given issue and date, each pivoted field name corresponds to at most one field_id.
evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over(partition by issue_id,field_id,cast(updated_at as date) order by updated_at desc) ... max(field_value) filter(where lower(field_name)='story points')
reason: Multiple IDs with the same pivot name can leave multiple selected values, making MAX choose text rather than the latest named-field change.

statement: Using a field-history date as open_until is valid for unresolved issues that have history.
evidence_of_dependence: coalesce(cast(valid_starting_on as date),current_date) open_until
alternative: The contract says "Set open_until to today if the issue is unresolved; otherwise to the calendar date of the field-history valid_starting_on".
reason: Ignoring resolution state can truncate unresolved issues' daily coverage to historical change windows.

statement: A resolved issue with no matching field-history row should use today as open_until.
evidence_of_dependence: coalesce(cast(valid_starting_on as date),current_date) open_until ... left join intermediate.int_jira__field_history_scd f using(issue_id)
alternative: The contract assigns resolved issues the field-history starting date and says "Only (issue_id, date_day) pairs that meet the window are emitted"; it specifies no fallback to today for missing resolved-issue history.
reason: The fallback can manufacture years of calendar rows for resolved issues without history.

statement: User activity consistency scores may retain DuckDB's inferred rounded numeric type instead of DOUBLE.
evidence_of_dependence: round(active_days_in_7d/7.0,3) consistency_score_7d,round(active_days_in_30d/30.0,3) consistency_score_30d
alternative: The contract declares both consistency_score columns as "data_type: DOUBLE".
reason: The expressions implement the numeric calculation but do not explicitly establish the documented output type.

statement: Explicit user_id and activity_date ordering is unnecessary for the user activity result.
evidence_of_dependence: at_churn_risk from win
alternative: The contract says "ordering is by user_id, activity_date (ordering does not affect values)".
reason: Window ordering does not guarantee the required final result ordering.
